Indeed, their record, in which their deeds that they used to do in the world were written, is ﴿in Sijjin﴾, which is the lowest, seventh earth. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Mughith ibn Sumayy, who said: ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾ He said: The lowest earth. He said: Iblis is bound with iron and chains in the lowest earth.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from Sulayman al-A'mash, from Shamir ibn Atiyyah, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: We were sitting with Ka'b, I and Rabi' ibn Khuthaym and Khalid ibn Ur'ur'a, and a group of our companions. Ka'b said: As for Sijjin, it is the lowest, seventh earth, and in it are the spirits of the disbelievers, beneath the limit of Iblis.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿in Sijjin﴾ He said: At the bottom of the seventh earth.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 83, verses 15–17:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay! Indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.(15) Then indeed they will burn in the Hellfire.(16) Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny."(17)﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: The matter is not as these deniers of the Day of Judgment say, that they have nearness (zulfa) with Allah. Indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord, so they will not see Him, nor will they see any of His honor reaching them.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is that they are veiled from His honor.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Khulayd, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Nay! Indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾: "He will not look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment."

Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, saying: Namran Abu al-Hasan al-Dhamari narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, that he used to say concerning this verse, ﴿Indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾: "They are the one who reminds people of his favors (mannan), the arrogant (mukhtal), and the one who seizes people's wealth with his oath by falsehood."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that they are veiled from seeing their Lord.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Razi narrated to me, saying: Abu Ma'mar al-Minqari narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Amr ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿Nay! Indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾: He said: "The veil will be lifted, and the believers will look at Him every day, morning and evening," or words to this effect.

The most correct of the sayings concerning this, with respect to the truth, is to say: Indeed Allah, exalted is He, informed about these people that they are veiled from seeing Him. It is possible that what is intended is veiling from His honor, and it is possible that what is intended is veiling from all of that, and there is no indication in the verse that shows that the veiling intended is from one meaning rather than another, nor is there any report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whose proof is established. So the correct position is to say: they are veiled from seeing Him, and from His honor, since the report is general, with no indication of its being specific.

And His words: ﴿in ʿIlliyyin﴾

Those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin﴾. It was mentioned to us that Kaʿb used to say: It is the right pillar of the Throne.

Kaʿb said: When the believing soul is taken, it is raised up, and the gates of heaven are opened for it, and the angels receive it with glad tidings. Then they ascend with it until they reach the Throne, and there is brought forth for it from beside the Throne a parchment which is inscribed, and then it is sealed with the recognition of its salvation on the Day of Judgment reckoning, and the angels brought near bear witness.

Others said: rather, by ʿIlliyyin is meant Paradise.

Those who said this:

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin﴾, he said: Paradise.

Others said: at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha).

Those who said this:

⁕ Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Bazuri, from the people of Kufa, narrated to me, saying: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, from al-Dahhak, who said: When the soul of the believing servant is taken, it is raised up to the heaven, and the brought-near ones set out with it to the second heaven. Al-Ajlah said: I said: And who are the brought-near ones? He said: The nearest of them to the second heaven. Then the brought-near ones set out with it to the third heaven, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, until it reaches the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. Al-Ajlah said: I said to al-Dahhak: Why is it called the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary? He said: Because everything of God's command ends at it and does not pass beyond it. Then it says: Lord, Your servant so-and-so, and He knows him better than they do; then God sends to them a sealed document that secures him from punishment. That is the saying of God: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin. And what can make you know what ʿIlliyyin is? It is a written record. Those brought near witness it.﴾

Others said: rather, by ʿIlliyyin is meant: in the heaven with God.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin﴾, he said: Their deeds are in a record with God in the heaven.

The correct view on this matter is to say that God, the Exalted, informed us that the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin. ʿIlliyyin is a plural whose meaning is: something above something, height upon height, and elevation after elevation. Therefore it takes the plural ending with yā' and nūn, like the plural of men, when it has no singular form with its dual, as has been related from some Arabs by hearing: "He fed us the broth of two broths" (aṭʿamanā marqata marqayn), meaning cooked meat. And as the poet said:

Qad rawayta illā al-Duhaydihīna... qulaysātin wa-ubaykirīnā

Then he said "wa-ubaykirīnā," pluralizing it with nūn, since he did not intend a specific number of virginities, but rather an unlimited number. And as another said:

Fa-asbahat al-madhāhibu qad adhāʿat... bihā al-iʿṣāru baʿda al-wābilīnā

Meaning: rain after rain, of unlimited number. Thus the Arabs do in every plural that has no singular or dual form, pluralizing it with nūn for both feminine and masculine, as we have explained. From this is their saying for men and women: ʿishrūn and thalāthūn. Given that this is as we have mentioned, it becomes clear that His words ﴿in ʿIlliyyin﴾ mean: in elevation and height, in a heaven above a heaven, height upon height. It is possible that this extends to the seventh heaven, to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and to the right pillar of the Throne, and there is no report that conclusively establishes that it refers to some of these rather than others.

The correct thing to say, as His, the Majestic's, words indicate, is that the record of the deeds of the righteous is in a height whose limit God, Majestic and Mighty, knows, while we have no knowledge of its ultimate end; yet it is not less than the seventh heaven, due to the consensus of the authoritative scholars of interpretation on this.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 83, verses 18–22:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin. And what can make you know what ʿIlliyyin is? It is a written record. Those brought near witness it. Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.﴾

His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin﴾. Al-abrar (the righteous) is the plural of barr, and they are those who are dutiful to God by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. Al-Hasan used to say: they are those who do not harm anything, not even an ant.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from a shaykh, from al-Hasan, who said: He was asked about the righteous, and he said: Those who do not harm an ant.

⁕ Ishaq ibn Zayd al-Khattabi narrated to us, saying: al-Firyabi narrated to us, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan, who said: The righteous are those who do not harm an ant.

And His words: ﴿in ʿIlliyyin﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of ʿIlliyyin. Some of them said: it is the seventh heaven.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from al-Aʿmash, from Shamir ibn ʿAtiyyah, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas asked Kaʿb, while I was present, about ʿIlliyyin. Others said: rather, by ʿIlliyyin is meant Paradise.

Those who said this:

⁕ Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Bazuri, from the people of Kufa, narrated to me, saying: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, from al-Dahhak, who said: When the soul of the believing servant is taken, it is raised up to the heaven, and the brought-near ones set out with it to the second heaven. Al-Ajlah said: I said: And who are the brought-near ones? He said: The nearest of them to the second heaven. Then the brought-near ones set out with it to the third heaven, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, until it reaches the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. Al-Ajlah said: I said to al-Dahhak: Why is it called the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary? He said: Because everything of God's command ends at it and does not pass beyond it. Then it says: Lord, Your servant so-and-so, and He knows him better than they do; then God sends to them a sealed document that secures him from punishment. That is the saying of God: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin. And what can make you know what ʿIlliyyin is? It is a written record. Those brought near witness it.﴾

Others said: rather, by ʿIlliyyin is meant: in the heaven with God.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin﴾, he said: Their deeds are in a record with God in the heaven.

The correct view on this matter is to say that God, the Exalted, informed us that the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin. ʿIlliyyin is a plural whose meaning is: something above something, height upon height, and elevation after elevation. Therefore it takes the plural ending with yā' and nūn, like the plural of men, when it has no singular form with its dual, as has been related from some Arabs by hearing: "He fed us the broth of two broths" (aṭʿamanā marqata marqayn), meaning cooked meat. And as the poet said:

Qad rawayta illā al-Duhaydihīna... qulaysātin wa-ubaykirīnā

Then he said "wa-ubaykirīnā," pluralizing it with nūn, since he did not intend a specific number of virginities, but rather an unlimited number. And as another said:

Fa-asbahat al-madhāhibu qad adhāʿat... bihā al-iʿṣāru baʿda al-wābilīnā

Meaning: rain after rain, of unlimited number. Thus the Arabs do in every plural that has no singular or dual form, pluralizing it with nūn for both feminine and masculine, as we have explained. From this is their saying for men and women: ʿishrūn and thalāthūn. Given that this is as we have mentioned, it becomes clear that His words ﴿in ʿIlliyyin﴾ mean: in elevation and height, in a heaven above a heaven, height upon height. It is possible that this extends to the seventh heaven, to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and to the right pillar of the Throne, and there is no report that conclusively establishes that it refers to some of these rather than others.

The correct thing to say, as His, the Majestic's, words indicate, is that the record of the deeds of the righteous is in a height whose limit God, Majestic and Mighty, knows, while we have no knowledge of its ultimate end; yet it is not less than the seventh heaven, due to the consensus of the authoritative scholars of interpretation on this.

Those who said that:

Have you not heard the women among you say: "Its perfume is such-and-such, mixed with musk"?

Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi related to me, saying: Ayyub related to us, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha', from someone he mentioned, from 'Alqama, regarding His words ﴿its seal is musk﴾, he said: Its mixture is musk.

He said: Waki' related to us, from his father, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha', from Yazid ibn Mu'awiya, from 'Alqama, regarding ﴿its seal is musk﴾, he said: its taste and its scent are musk.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that the last of their drink is sealed with musk placed in it.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿its seal is musk﴾, he said: Its outcome is musk; the people's drink is blended for them with camphor and sealed with musk.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿its seal is musk﴾, he said: Its outcome is musk.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Hatim ibn Wardan related to us, saying: Abu Hamza related to us, from Ibrahim and al-Hasan, regarding this verse ﴿its seal is musk﴾, he said: Its outcome is musk.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: Abu Hamza related to us, from Jabir, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Abu al-Darda', regarding ﴿its seal is musk﴾: the drink is white like silver, and they seal their drink with it; and if a man of the world inserted his finger into it and then withdrew it, no living being would remain without finding its fragrance.

Others said: By His words ﴿sealed﴾ is meant ﴿plastered﴾, ﴿its seal is musk﴾: its plaster is musk.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿sealed, its seal is musk﴾, he said: Its plaster is musk.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿sealed﴾, "wine"; ﴿its seal is musk﴾: its seal in the sight of God is musk, while its seal today in the world is clay.

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the opinion of the one who said: the meaning of that is: its last part and its outcome is musk, meaning that it is good in scent, and that its scent at the end of their drinking is sealed with the scent of musk.

We said that this is the most correct of these views because there is no sense of "sealing" in the speech of the Arabs except closing and finishing, as when they say: "So-and-so completed the Qur'an," meaning he reached its end. Since there is no sense in sealing the drink of the people of Paradise, given that their drink flows like water in rivers, and is not aged in jars that are then sealed with clay, it becomes clear that the correct meaning is the other one: the outcome and the last part of the drink, which is what the drink is sealed with. As for "sealing" in the sense of mixing, we do not know of it being heard in the speech of the Arabs.

The reciters differed in reading this. The reciters of the major regions read ﴿khitamuhu misk﴾, except al-Kisa'i, who read it ﴿khatamahu misk﴾.

The correct reading in our view is that of the reciters of the major regions, namely ﴿khitamuhu﴾, since the authoritative reciters agreed upon it. Although al-khitam and al-khatam differ in form, they are close in meaning, except that al-khatam is a noun while al-khitam is a verbal noun. From it comes the line of al-Farazdaq:

So they spent the night beside me, felled, and I spent the night breaking open the seals of the sealing.

A parallel to this is their saying: "He has noble natures and characters."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 83, verse 35–36:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Upon couches, looking.﴾ ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿So today those who believed, from among the disbelievers, will laugh﴾, and that is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿upon couches, looking﴾. He says: upon their thrones which are in the canopies, looking at them while they are in Paradise, and the disbelievers are being punished in the Fire.

And those who engage in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So today those who believed, from among the disbelievers, will laugh upon couches, looking﴾. He said: It means the raised thrones upon which are canopies. Ibn 'Abbas used to say: Between Paradise and the Fire there is a wall in which doors are opened for them, so the believers look at the people of the Fire, and the believers on the thrones look at how they are being punished, and they laugh at them. That is among what Allah gives coolness to their eyes with, seeing how Allah takes vengeance upon them.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So today those who believed, from among the disbelievers, will laugh﴾. It was mentioned to us that Ka'b used to say: Between Paradise and the Fire there are windows. When a believer wishes to look at an enemy he had in the world, he looks out from one of the windows. Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning in the middle of the Fire. It was also mentioned to us that he saw the skulls of the people boiling.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Ka'b said: Between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire there are windows; no man of Paradise wishes to look at another of the people of the Fire except that he does so.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿So today those who believed, from among the disbelievers, will laugh upon couches, looking﴾: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: The wall is between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, and doors are opened for the people of Paradise, so they look, while on the thrones, at the people of the Fire, how they are being punished, and they laugh at them. That is among what Allah gives coolness to their eyes with, seeing how Allah takes vengeance upon them.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿So today those who believed, from among the disbelievers, will laugh﴾. He said: The disbelievers will be brought until they look at the people of Paradise in Paradise, on thrones. When they look at them, the doors will be closed between them, and the people of Paradise will laugh at them. That is His saying: ﴿So today those who believed, from among the disbelievers, will laugh upon couches, looking﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Have the disbelievers been rewarded and recompensed for the reward of what they used to do in the world to the believers, of mocking them and laughing at them, by the laughter of the believers at them in the Hereafter, while the believers are upon couches looking, and they are in the Fire being punished?

And ﴿thuwwiba﴾ is a verb from reward and recompense; it is said of it: thawwaba fulanun fulanan 'ala sani'ihi, and athabahu minhu (he rewarded him for his deed, and recompensed him for it).

And those who engage in interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ He said: Recompensed.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ When they used to mock.

End of the commentary on Surah Al-Mutaffifin.
